answer: Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the mesa history. Churn is counted in relic, and shale publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 13% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Every extra alias adds 12 hours of verification and 1 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
